title: KRAMABENCH: A Benchmark for AI Systems on Data-to-Insight Pipelines over Data Lakes
claim: A realistic question requires orchestrating many data tasks across a messy, heterogeneous data lake to reach a single answer.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; task box, thought-cloud task hints, data lake panel
description: The figure is a left-to-right illustration of one benchmark task. On the left, a gray rounded box holds the natural-language task: find the total money defrauded in 2024 according to the Consumer Sentinel Network, as an integer in millions of dollars. In the middle, three thought clouds (Data discovery, Table Extraction, Data Cleaning) sit above a lightbulb. Arrows from the task and from the data lake both point at the lightbulb, and a blue callout under it reads '5435 million'. On the right, a large rounded Data Lake panel holds simplified file snippets in different colors: a green Municipalities table, a pink text note about the Consumer Sentinel Network, a blue transaction table with a footnote, and an orange Fraud by Municipalities table. Document icons sit at the edge. The eye goes first to the task text, then to the lightbulb.
caption: One of the tasks of \ourbenchmark based on a real data lake of 136 files in the legal discovery domain. Data file sample snippets are simplified.
abstract: Discovering insights from a real-world data lake potentially containing unclean, semi-structured, and unstructured data requires a variety of data processing tasks, ranging from extraction and cleaning to integration, analysis, and modeling. This process often also demands domain knowledge and project-specific insight. While AI models have shown remarkable results in reasoning and code generation, their abilities to design and execute complex pipelines that solve these data-lake-to-insight challenges remain unclear. We introduce KramaBench which consists of 104 manually curated and solved challenges spanning 1700 files, 24 data sources, and 6 domains. KramaBench focuses on testing the end-to-end capabilities of AI systems to solve challenges which require automated orchestration of different data tasks. KramaBench also features a comprehensive evaluation framework assessing the pipeline design and individual data task implementation abilities of AI systems. We evaluate 8 LLMs using our single-agent reference framework DS-Guru, alongside both open- and closed-source single- and multi-agent systems, and find that while current agentic systems may handle isolated data-science tasks and generate plausible draft pipelines, they struggle with producing working end-to-end pipelines. On KramaBench, the best system reaches only 55% end-to-end accuracy in the full data-lake setting. Even with perfect retrieval, the accuracy tops out at 62%. Leading LLMs can identify up to 42% of important data tasks but can only fully implement 20% of individual data tasks. Our code, reference framework, and data are available at https://github.com/mitdbg/KramaBench.
